fresh box: no config · run 'caramelo commander init' to name this machine

A peer is an identity — a laptop, an agent, a CI runner — admitted to
the machine's private network by its WireGuard public key. The machine never
answers a packet from a key it does not know, and every command that arrives
through the tunnel is logged under the peer's name.

'caramelo vpn up' adds the commander as a peer; these commands are for adding
the others.

Usage:
  caramelo peer [flags]

Examples:
  caramelo peer add agent-7 <public key>
  caramelo peer list
  caramelo peer remove agent-7


Flags:
  -h, --help   help for peer

Global Flags:
      --fleet string      fleet to talk to, by its name in the commander config (default: the app's fleet, then the default fleet)
      --json              print machine-readable JSON on stdout
      --machine string    raw ssh target to talk to, for a machine that is in no fleet yet: user@host[:port], or 'local'
      --progress string   how progress is written to stderr: text (default) or json, one event per line

3 commands are hidden here; 'caramelo manual --role all' lists every command of every role.
